John Naples was a captain and first-team regional honoree for Saugus High in 1958. The Item's North Shore All-Star roster selected him at guard and identified him as a senior. His captaincy and selection recognized the line play behind Saugus football in the late 1950s.

He was also named in the lineup of the Lynn–Swampscott All-Stars for their 14–6 victory over Salem–Beverly in the third annual Harry Agganis Memorial game at Manning Bowl on December 7, 1958. The Globe’s game report listed Naples among the winning side’s guards.

The Boston Globe additionally included Naples among its All-Scholastic honorable mentions at guard in December 1958.

alumni.bio: Ron “Ronnie” Barressi captained the 1964 Sachems. alumni.name: John Dancewicz
alumni.bio:
John Dancewicz was a co-captain of Saugus High's 7–2 football team in 1966 and a first-team Lynn Item All-Star. He also scored in the 48–0 Thanksgiving shutout of Peabody. The Item honored his line play at tackle, while the yearbook also identifies him as a back. Dancewicz also served as senior class president and appears among the year's National Merit finalists, giving his profile a documented combination of football leadership and academic accomplishment.

A 1967 newspaper profile identifies his two-way roles more specifically as offensive tackle and defensive linebacker. Dancewicz won the 1966 Thom McAn Trophy. He also became the first New England student to receive the national $1,000 scholarship associated with the Thom McAn football trophy. Selected from players representing more than 850 teams, he was recognized for sportsmanship, scholarship, teamwork, leadership and competitive spirit, together with his essay on attending college. He ranked third in his class of 350 and was the nephew of Notre Dame All-American Boley Dancewicz. The Globe also listed him among its 1966 All-Scholastic honorable mentions at tackle.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Mancuso
alumni.bio:
Jim Mancuso was a first-team Lynn Item All-Star tackle on Saugus High's successful 1966 team. The newspaper listed him at 6-foot-1 and 205 pounds, and the yearbook preserves his individual football portrait. His senior biography records four years of football and hockey and identifies him as a hockey co-captain. Mancuso combined individual football recognition with participation across several sports.

Mancuso earned a further regional distinction when the Globe’s August 18, 1967 Agganis preview listed him as a projected starting guard for the North squad at Manning Bowl. The article identified the University of Connecticut as his intended college.

alumni.name: Edward “Eddie” Maguire
alumni.bio:
Edward Maguire was a backfield leader and co-captain of Saugus High's 7–2 team in 1966. He earned first-team Lynn Item All-Star recognition at back, joining teammates John Dancewicz and Jim Mancuso on the selected team. The yearbook preserves his co-captain portrait alongside Dancewicz and Paul Uga, documenting the leadership group behind one of Saugus's strongest seasons of the decade.

He ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns in a 33–6 season-opening win over B.C. High. He also scored against Marblehead after Jim Paolini’s interception set up the drive in a 29–0 shutout.

The Globe named Maguire an All-Scholastic honorable mention at back in 1966, and its August 18, 1967 Agganis preview listed him as a projected North starting halfback, with Indiana as his intended college.

At Indiana University, he moved to defensive end and earned football letters in 1969 and 1970. Indiana’s official record book credits him with 17 tackles for loss in each season, for a career total of 34, and lists him as a second-team All-Big Ten selection in 1970. These college achievements add a major-conference defensive career to his Saugus backfield accomplishments.

Eddie Koschei put Maguire among the hardest-running Saugus backs he had watched, behind Ed Shipulski, in Bob Walsh’s Item retrospective.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Fauci
alumni.bio: James Fauci captained Saugus High during Buzz Harvey's first season as head coach in 1937. His senior yearbook praised his alert, determined play and the example he set for his teammates. The team opened with five consecutive victories over Marblehead, Barnstable, Gloucester, Amesbury and Woburn and finished 7–2–1. Its yearbook celebrated the opening win over traditional rival Marblehead and the strong start under Harvey; the Thanksgiving finale against Danvers ended in a 6–6 tie. His yearbook tribute preserves an important leadership figure from the late 1930s.

alumni.bio: Earl Hanson was a three-season football participant and captain of Saugus High's 1938 team. His senior yearbook remembered a quiet leader whose courage helped set the tone for his teammates. The Sachems finished 6–4 and closed with a 6–0 Thanksgiving victory over Danvers. Hanson's captaincy links the early years of Buzz Harvey's program with the greater success that followed in 1939.

Michael Light was a co-captain of Saugus High's 1958 football team and earned second-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition at end. His senior biography records three seasons of football and four years of hockey, preserving the range of his athletic participation. Light shared the football captaincy with John Naples.

He was also named in the lineup of the Lynn–Swampscott All-Stars for their 14–6 victory over Salem–Beverly in the third annual Harry Agganis Memorial game at Manning Bowl on December 7, 1958. The Globe’s game report listed Light among the winning side’s ends.

alumni.name: David Russell “Dave” Mathews
alumni.bio:
David Russell “Dave” Mathews, Saugus High Class of 1960, was a football co-captain and quarterback on the Sachems’ recognized 1959 championship team. The Lynn Item named him a first-team North Shore football All-Star at back in 1959. A four-year participant in football, he was among the final graduating players to compete under longtime Saugus coach John Janusas. His senior yearbook and the team’s portrait collection preserve his leadership and broad athletic ability.

Mathews helped deliver a memorable 14–6 Thanksgiving victory over Peabody in 1959 before approximately 8,500 fans at Stackpole Field. He threw the first-period touchdown pass to end Frank Bucchiere and ran for the two-point conversion, giving Saugus an 8–0 lead. The victory spoiled Peabody’s Class A title opportunity. The Globe also listed D. R. Mathews among its 1959 All-Scholastic honorable mentions at back.

Mathews also excelled in hockey and baseball. A hockey co-captain and four-year participant in both sports, he earned Essex County League hockey All-Star recognition three times and was Saugus’s leading hockey scorer, according to The Saugus Advocate’s retrospective. The Saugus High School Alumni Association’s July 2011 newsletter identifies him in the photograph of the 1959–60 championship hockey team.

His athletic career continued beyond Saugus: The Saugus Advocate reports that he was heavily recruited and went on to play hockey at Boston College. His college seasons, statistics and honors have not yet been established by the sources reviewed.

Mathews was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 1989. The Advocate later included him among its “Terrific Twenty-Five” Saugus Hall of Famers, recognizing his achievements across football, hockey and baseball.

Eddie Koschei gave Mathews honorable mention at quarterback and ranked him with Chris Serino just behind Mike Harrington among Saugus’s all-around athletes in Bob Walsh’s Item retrospective.

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Burt
alumni.bio:
Richard Burt was a fullback on Saugus High's recognized 1959 championship team and earned second-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition. His senior biography records four years each of football and baseball and specifically praises his running for the champion football team. The yearbook's award list also names him as recipient of the John A. W. Pearce Football Award. Burt combined team success with regional recognition and a school football award.

Burt scored the winning touchdown in the 1959 Thanksgiving upset of Peabody. After Saugus stopped a fourth-down pass at the Peabody 20 in the fourth quarter, the Sachems drove for the decisive score, with Burt carrying over from the one-yard line. The 14–6 victory, watched by approximately 8,500 fans, denied Peabody a chance at the Class A title.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Louis “Lou” O’Neil
alumni.bio:
Louis O'Neil was a four-year football participant and captain whose line play earned first-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition in 1968. His senior biography also lists hockey, track and weightlifting, reflecting his broad athletic involvement. The 1969 yearbook's football roster identifies him as a captain during a season in which Saugus recovered from a difficult start to finish with three consecutive victories. His first-team selection recognized his line play at the end of the decade.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Canole
alumni.bio: James Canole was a captain and three-season football participant at Saugus High. The Item named him to its 1968 North Shore All-Star second team as a utility player. His senior biography also records track, volleyball and gymnastics participation, while the football section preserves his captaincy and role in the team's late-season improvement. His regional recognition and leadership marked his contribution to the Class of 1969.

alumni.name: Robert “Bob” Osgood
alumni.bio:
At Saugus, Osgood earned first-team Lynn Item All-Star recognition at back and first-team Northeastern Conference offensive honors in 1969. He completed 54 passes for 1,157 yards and eight touchdowns and earned Boston Globe Class B All-Star and All-Scholastic bench recognition. In a 28–26 win over Newburyport that moved Saugus to 5–0, he completed six passes for 259 yards and three touchdowns. In a 30–6 win over Winthrop, he threw a 99-yard touchdown to John Richard. Against Watertown, he passed for a touchdown and two conversions to Greg Manship and ran for another score. He quarterbacked a 7–2 team whose only losses came against Class A champion Peabody and Class B champion Swampscott. He was then selected as one of the North squad’s quarterbacks for the 1970 Harry Agganis All-Star game. A Globe pregame feature described him as a drop-back passer being coached to add roll-out plays against the South’s heavier defensive line.

Bob Osgood, Saugus High Class of 1970, quarterbacked the Sachems before continuing his football career at the University of New Hampshire. The Saugus Advocate’s retrospective describes him as heavily recruited and identifies him as a starting quarterback at UNH. The university’s own archives confirm his membership on the 1973 football team under head coach Bill Bowes, identifying him by name in the team photograph. His complete college football seasons, individual statistics and starting assignments remain to be established from contemporary records.

Osgood was also an accomplished basketball and baseball player at Saugus. He played three years of high-school basketball and was a right-handed pitcher on Saugus’s 1970 state-tournament baseball team. His two-sport college career is supported by UNH’s archives, which identify him in both the 1971 and 1972 baseball team photographs. The Advocate remembers him as an outstanding pitcher at UNH as well as a college quarterback.

He was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 1990. The Saugus Advocate later included him among its “Terrific Twenty-Five” Saugus Hall of Famers.

alumni.name: Raphael Zammit
alumni.source: Newspaper clippings and college records. Contributed 1997 newspaper scoring summaries. 2004 Shriners Football Classic program · p. 106.
alumni.bio:
As a junior in 1997, Zammit scored on a 75-yard kickoff return against Danvers and a 65-yard catch against Swampscott. The available scoring summaries document nine touchdowns that fall, including five catches, three runs and the kickoff return.

Senior captain Raphael Zammit earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic honors at tailback and strong safety in 1998, along with Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors. He rushed for 1,481 yards and 21 rushing touchdowns, a school record at the time. He scored 25 total touchdowns and led Division 3 with 154 points. He closed the season with three rushing touchdowns and a 25-yard touchdown catch in a 39–32 Thanksgiving loss at Peabody. Justin Winn broke the rushing touchdown record with 22 in 2014. The Item reports 2,452 all-purpose yards and the Globe reports 2,453. On defense, he had 52 tackles, eight sacks and three interceptions, returning one for a touchdown. The Globe credited him with 2,891 rushing yards, 4,653 all-purpose yards and 41 touchdowns over his Saugus career. He was named South MVP in the 1999 Agganis All-Star game.

At Curry College from 2000 through 2003, Zammit rushed for 4,353 career yards and 44 touchdowns. He earned second-team all-conference honors in 2000 and 2001, then first-team honors and conference Offensive Player of the Year in 2002 and 2003. As a junior in 2002, he was named a third-team running back on the Hewlett Packard Division III All-America team. Curry’s records also list third-team All-America honors in 2003. He rushed for 1,479 yards in 2002 and 1,587 in 2003.

Raphael Zammit represented Saugus in the 1999 Shriners Football Classic.

alumni.name: Marvens Jean
alumni.bio:
As a junior in 2018, Marvens Jean rushed for 266 yards as sixth-seeded Saugus beat third-seeded Weston 27–6 on the road in the Division 5 North quarterfinals. He earned Lynn Item All-Star recognition as a senior in 2019, contributing as both a runner and defensive back. His senior profile records 1,074 rushing yards, 12 rushing touchdowns, 87 tackles, two forced fumbles and a kickoff return for a touchdown.

At UMass Dartmouth, his roster career spanned 2020–2024 and included both running back and wide receiver. He earned second-team All-MASCAC honors in 2021 after rushing for 772 yards and five touchdowns, then ran for 254 yards against Husson in 2022. Moving to wide receiver in 2023, he caught 42 passes for 544 yards. Back at running back in 2024, he rushed for 540 yards over the season and contributed 79 yards and a touchdown in the MASCAC title-clinching victory over Plymouth State.

alumni.name: Dan Cacciola
alumni.bio:
Dan Cacciola set Saugus’s single-game rushing record with 375 yards and four touchdowns against Winthrop in 2014, in the season opener. The Boston Globe reported that all four touchdowns came on runs of more than 60 yards, including a 99-yarder.

The Boston Globe reported 650 rushing yards as a junior in 2013, despite a leg injury that cost him four games. His senior season produced 1,467 rushing yards and 18 rushing touchdowns in the Item’s season profile. He earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors, together with Boston Globe Eastern Massachusetts Division 4 All-Star recognition. Alongside fellow runner Justin Winn, Cacciola helped Saugus finish 6–5 in 2014. His school record and recognition from several selectors make him a standout of that era.

alumni.name: George Lowe
alumni.bio:
George Lowe was a captain and Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star during Saugus’s 1999 season. His senior Item profile credits him with 604 rushing yards, 27 catches for 148 yards, 72 tackles, four interceptions and two fumble recoveries. He scored nine touchdowns, including three in a 30–14 win over Marblehead and one on an 85-yard kickoff return against Salem. As a younger player in 1997, Lowe threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to Mike Panzini in a win over Lynn Classical.

He continued at Curry College as a cornerback. In 2003, he earned first-team all-conference and second-team ECAC All-Region honors. Curry’s record book credits him with 13 passes broken up that season, tied for second on the school’s season leaderboard when the book was updated in January 2025.

alumni.name: Paul Nigro
alumni.bio:
Paul Nigro was a senior captain and Lynn Item All-Star in 1978. His senior capsule credits him with 1,395 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns, complemented by 25 receptions for 360 yards and 14 kickoff returns for 207 yards.

Nigro’s combination of running, receiving and return work gave Saugus a versatile offensive threat. His preserved Item profile documents one of the program’s notable individual rushing seasons of the late 1970s.

Nigro also starred for Saugus High in ice hockey as a forward. In 1977–78, he recorded 21 goals and 21 assists for 42 points, leading the Northeastern Conference in scoring according to the Massachusetts high school tournament program. In 1978–79, he added 15 goals and 24 assists for 39 points. His documented two-season totals were 36 goals, 45 assists and 81 points. Elite Prospects lists him atop its Saugus High all-time recorded points table.

The Boston Globe documented several of Nigro’s standout performances. In the 25–0 upset of favored Winthrop, the 5-foot-11, 192-pound senior rushed for 152 yards on 16 carries and scored three touchdowns, including an 87-yard opening kickoff return. Against Lynn English, he rushed for 271 yards on just eight carries in the first quarter, scoring on two long runs and an 83-yard touchdown reception for 354 total offensive yards; he had reached 13 season touchdowns at that point. In the Thanksgiving finale, he rushed for 165 yards and scored three touchdowns, including a 66-yard run, to lead a 30–14 win over Peabody. The Globe described him as one of Eastern Massachusetts’ top halfbacks.

New Haven’s 1983 football roster lists Nigro as a senior tailback from Saugus High. The Chargers’ all-time football roster also lists him for 1983.

Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1991.

alumni.name: Frank Mancuso
alumni.bio: Frank Mancuso was a Saugus tri-captain and a 1973 Lynn Item All-Star interior lineman. Listed at 6-foot-1 and 205 pounds, he played tackle on both sides of the ball before shifting to offensive guard, and also saw action at defensive end. His Item profile credits him with 14 quarterback sacks and reports that his coaches rated him highest on the squad in all but one game. His pass rush and versatility made him a standout on the Sachems’ line.

alumni.name: Steve Spinney
alumni.bio:
Steve Spinney captained the 1974 Sachems and earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star recognition. The Item selected the 6-foot-2, 215-pound senior at offensive end and highlighted his versatility, noting that he played many positions. He helped lead Saugus to a 6–4 season under Mike Ginolfi. He returned an interception 39 yards for the deciding touchdown in the 12–7 win at Marblehead and caught a two-point pass in the win over Lynn Classical.

Steve is the son of fellow Saugus football great Art Spinney, Class of 1945, who captained Boston College and became an All-Pro lineman and two-time NFL champion with the Baltimore Colts. The contemporary Item profile explicitly identifies their father–son relationship, connecting two generations of Sachems football.

Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1994.

alumni.bio:
Colt Meredith’s football career culminated in national recognition at Plymouth State. The contributed 1993 Saugus preview identifies him as a senior, establishing his Saugus graduation class as 1994.

He played linebacker and defensive back for Plymouth State from 1996 through 1999 and captained the team in 1999. That fall, he was named Freedom Football Conference Defensive Player of the Year and earned Hewlett-Packard/SID Division III All-America honorable mention as a defensive back. His conference award, college captaincy and national recognition distinguish his career beyond Saugus.

alumni.name: Ryan Leahy
alumni.bio:
Ryan Leahy quarterbacked the Sachems from 1996 through 1998 and co-captained the 1998 team. As a sophomore in 1996, Leahy threw at least seven touchdown passes, including an 89-yarder to L.J. McKanas against Salem. As a junior in 1997, he completed 65 of 124 passes for 1,109 yards and 14 touchdowns and ran 35 times for 294 yards and four more scores. He accounted for four touchdowns in a 31–8 win over Danvers and threw the fourth-quarter winner to Chris McBride in a 24–20 victory at Salem. He helped Saugus finish 6–4–1 and earned Daily Evening Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors at quarterback.

Leahy earned a second NEC All-Star selection in 1998. Entering the Thanksgiving finale against Peabody, he had completed 43 of 82 passes for 825 yards and seven touchdowns, rushed for five touchdowns and also played free safety. He threw for two more touchdowns in the finale, a 25-yarder to Raphael Zammit and a 30-yarder to Mike Lush, bringing his documented senior totals to at least 880 passing yards and nine touchdown passes. The Boston Globe later credited him with 30 career touchdown passes, tying him for 25th on its historical Massachusetts list. Saugus newspaper records credit Steve Peach with 33 career touchdown passes across his three varsity seasons.

After Saugus, Leahy was listed as a 5-foot-11, 170-pound wide receiver for Bentley College football in a contemporary newspaper clipping.

alumni.name: Kyle Sucharewicz
alumni.bio:
Kyle Sucharewicz quarterbacked the Sachems at the turn of the millennium. As a sophomore in 1999, he scored on a 14-yard run in the fourth quarter to beat Methuen 6–0. He threw touchdown passes of 65 yards to George Lowe and 10 yards to Mike Navarro in a 20–12 win over Swampscott. That fall, he earned Northeastern Conference and Eastern Massachusetts Division 3 All-Star honors at quarterback.

In 2000, Sucharewicz threw three touchdown passes in a 26–6 win at Marblehead, finding Mark Pizzotti, Patrick Eaton and Tom Shidlow. He also threw to Adam Magnasco for a two-point conversion. As a senior in 2001, he threw three touchdown passes as Saugus rallied from a 14–0 deficit to beat Salem 30–14.

Sucharewicz scored 1,180 career points for Saugus basketball from 1998 to 2002. The Saugus Advocate’s February 2026 scoring list ranked him second among Saugus boys, behind Alex Winn, and third on the combined boys’ and girls’ list. He returned to Saugus as a basketball coach. A 2014 profile reported that he had spent the previous five years as a varsity assistant and head junior varsity coach. He entered the Saugus High School Sports Hall of Fame in 2014 for football and basketball.

Accolades and milestones
• 1999 Northeastern Conference Football All-Star at quarterback
• 1999 Eastern Massachusetts Division 3 Football All-Star at quarterback
• Saugus basketball 1,000-point club, with 1,180 career points
• 2014 Saugus High School Sports Hall of Fame inductee for football and basketball

The Beverly preview credited him with 129 passing yards against Salem. He found Mark Pizzotti twice for touchdowns, including the go-ahead score with 1:18 remaining.

alumni.name: George Nicolo
alumni.bio:
George Nicolo quarterbacked the Sachems during their 1977 Northeastern Conference championship season under head coach Mike Ginolfi. Saugus finished 9–1 and won the conference championship. Nicolo’s senior season stands as the school’s single-season passing-touchdown record: 15 touchdown passes. Contemporary season statistics credit him with 1,052 passing yards on 81 completions in 157 attempts, plus four successful conversion passes. He also scored two rushing touchdowns. He ran for one score and threw to Frank Serino for the other in a 12–0 upset of defending Division 3 Super Bowl champion Lynn Classical. He connected with Serino again for the fourth-quarter winner in the 12–10 Thanksgiving victory over Peabody that clinched the NEC title outright. The 15 passing touchdowns led Massachusetts Division II according to the contemporary season leaders chart. As a junior varsity quarterback in 1975, Nicolo threw four touchdown passes in a 26–8 win over Salem the week his cousin John helped the varsity rally past Salem. He found Frank Serino for scores of 60 and 20 yards and Keith Manning twice from 10 yards.

His 1977 performances earned Lynn Item All-Star recognition at quarterback and selection to the Northeastern Conference offensive All-Star team. Nicolo was among the key players on one of the Sachems’ most successful teams of the 1970s. Saugus High School inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1996.

Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1996.

alumni.name: John “Sal” Nicolo
alumni.bio:
John “Sal” Nicolo played football for Saugus High from 1999 through 2002 and graduated in 2003. He started at fullback and linebacker in 2001 and 2002 under his father, the Sachems’ head coach.

As a junior, Nicolo scored on a five-yard run against Danvers. On Thanksgiving against Peabody, Nicolo sparked Saugus’s comeback bid when he intercepted quarterback Mike Shah just before halftime and returned it 33 yards for a touchdown. His third-quarter fumble recovery gave the Sachems another chance, but the offense threw three straight incompletions and had to punt. Peabody pulled away, and Nicolo earned a Lynn Item Top Performers mention for his defensive play. As a senior, he intercepted a pass in the opener at Belmont, rushed for more than 50 yards and scored from two yards out at Danvers, and ran for a touchdown against Gloucester. His 35-yard fumble return deep into Marblehead territory helped spark a 31–16 Saugus win. On Thanksgiving 2002, he tackled Peabody’s Matt Williams in the backfield to stop a two-point try. The Agganis Foundation selected him for the 2003 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic. He wore No. 31 for the South in its 24–14 win at Manning Bowl.

Nicolo joined the varsity wrestling program as a sophomore in 2000–01, won a match at 140 pounds in an early quad meet, and earned the team’s Rookie of the Year award. He went on to record pins against Somerville, Watertown and Minuteman and won a 152-pound decision at the Whittier Tech Tournament. He also competed in track for Saugus.

After graduation, he played linebacker at Bridgewater State College under Peter Mazzaferro in 2003 and 2004. Bridgewater’s records list him as John Nicolo (No. 38) in 2003, when he appeared in two games and recorded one solo tackle, and as Sal Nicolo (No. 55) in 2004, when he appeared in one game.

As a junior on Thanksgiving 2001, he returned a Mike Shah interception 33 yards for a touchdown and recovered a Peabody fumble. The Item included him in its weekly Top Performers roundup.
alumni.source: Sal’s Scrapbook and contributed game and wrestling clippings, the Nicolo family history and researcher profile, Agganis selection coverage, and Bridgewater State participation records.

alumni.name: Rodney Lavoie
alumni.bio: The 2006 captain led Saugus to a 13–0 Thanksgiving win over Peabody, its first victory over the Tanners in 18 years. The Boston Globe credited him with 186 yards on 35 carries, while the Lynn Item listed 184 rushing yards. The Sachems won their final three games after an 0–7 start. His Lynn Item All-Star profile credited him with more than 1,000 all-purpose yards and three touchdowns in the 43–0 win over Holyoke Catholic/Granby. He earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors as a senior. In 2015, Lavoie finished fourth on CBS’s Survivor: Worlds Apart.

alumni.name: Tyler Trainor
alumni.bio: The 2007 captain anchored the defense on Saugus’s first winning team since 1997. The Lynn Item credited him with 108 tackles, three forced fumbles and two interceptions, one returned for a touchdown. It also reported that he averaged more than eight yards per carry and scored five touchdowns on offense as the Sachems finished 7–3. Trainor earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors, the Walter Boverini Defensive Player of the Year award and the Saugus Lions Club Heisman Trophy. He went on to play linebacker and safety at Bridgewater State from 2008 through 2011. Plymouth State’s box scores document his game appearances in 2010 and 2011.

alumni.name: Mike Dean
alumni.bio: Dean helped power consecutive 7–3 seasons under coach Mike Broderick and shared the captaincy with Bret Reid in 2008. The Lynn Item credited Dean with 1,242 rushing yards on 130 carries and 17 touchdowns as a senior. Its profile also reported two interception returns for touchdowns. He earned NEC recognition in 2007 and returned as an NEC Small All-Star in 2008, when he also earned Lynn Item and Eastern Massachusetts Division 3 All-Star honors. Dean played defensive back at UMass Dartmouth in 2009 and 2010. He started at free safety against Curry as a freshman.

alumni.name: Tommy Trainor
alumni.bio: Trainor captained the 2012 Sachems and anchored the defense at middle linebacker. The Lynn Item credited him with 110 tackles, including seven for loss, as Saugus improved to 6–5 and shut out Peabody 43–0 on Thanksgiving. He earned Lynn Item and CAL/NEC All-Star honors and received the Saugus Heisman Trophy at the pre-Thanksgiving dinner. The Boston Globe profiled three generations of his football family. His father Tom and uncle Don, both former Sachems linebackers, were on the Saugus coaching staff. Bridgewater State listed Tommy as a freshman linebacker in 2013.

alumni.name: Tommy DeSimone
alumni.bio: A captain on the 2023 team, DeSimone rushed for 1,113 yards and 14 touchdowns as Saugus opened 3–0 and finished 5–6. He ran 28 times for 140 yards and three touchdowns in a 28–22 win over Northeast, earning a Boston Globe Player of the Week mention. He also scored Saugus’s touchdown on a 13-yard run against Peabody on Thanksgiving. DeSimone earned Lynn Item honors at running back and was named Northeastern Conference Offensive All-Conference. In 2026, he played linebacker for Worcester State and recorded five tackles and two sacks against Dean College.

alumni.name: Patrick “Pat” Eaton
alumni.bio:
Eaton captained the 2001 Sachems and contributed as a runner, receiver and defensive back. His senior Lynn Item profile credits him with 545 rushing yards and 30 catches for 505 yards, for 1,050 yards from scrimmage. The game accounts include a 48-yard touchdown catch against Lynn Classical and a 19-yard touchdown run against Marblehead. As a junior in 2000, he ran for touchdowns of 72 and 10 yards against Danvers and caught a 31-yard touchdown pass against Winthrop. Eaton earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference football All-Star honors, and the season archive records his selection for the 2002 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic.

In the 2001 comeback at Salem, Eaton returned a kickoff 53 yards, caught a touchdown and ran in three two-point conversions. He ran for 87 yards on 19 carries in the win over Marblehead.

alumni.name: Pat Quinlan
alumni.bio:
Quinlan started for four years on defense at Saugus and was a senior captain, according to the Boston Globe. He contributed on offense as well. In 2000, he scored both Saugus touchdowns in a 13–10 win at Swampscott, including the go-ahead 60-yard run. He also ran for a touchdown and a two-point conversion against Winthrop that fall. The Item’s Thanksgiving preview reported that Quinlan and Pat Eaton had combined for 1,200 rushing yards, and coach Dean Sacca singled out Quinlan for his consistency on offense. The archive lists him as a 2002 Harry Agganis football All-Star. His father, Fred “Freddie” Quinlan (Saugus High Class of 1972), played on the line at Saugus and earned All-American honors at Plymouth State. His grandfather, Fred Quinlan (Saugus High Class of 1950), was a running back on the 1949 Exchange Bowl champions and a catcher for the Sachems.

Quinlan played at Plymouth State from 2002 through 2005, moving from linebacker to the defensive line and captaining the Panthers as a senior. In 2004, he received the Fred Madore Award and the Jason D. Holder Award as Homecoming MVP. The Globe reported 35 tackles, seven for loss, in his senior season. His two blocked extra points helped preserve a 21–19 win over Husson and earned him a spot on the D3football.com Team of the Week.

In the 18–7 win over Marblehead in 2001, Quinlan scored from the 1 behind a block by Nick Picozzi. The Thanksgiving recap identifies him as a senior fullback and defensive end.
alumni.source: Boston Globe feature, Saugus season archive and Plymouth State football records.

alumni.name: Fred Quinlan
alumni.bio:
A running back in football and a catcher in baseball, Fred Quinlan made his mark at Saugus High in both sports. In 1947, he broke a 66-yard touchdown run in a 14–6 win over Marblehead. Two years later, he scored 10 regular-season touchdowns for John Janusas’s Sachems, who shared the North Shore title with Gloucester and finished 10–1 after beating Weymouth 7–6 in the Exchange Bowl. The Lynn Item named him All-Scholastic as a utility player, and the Boston Globe gave him All-Scholastic honorable mention as a back.

In the 27–13 Thanksgiving win over Peabody in 1948, Quinlan caught Sardi Nicolo’s pass after defender Andy Thain deflected it near the goal line. The Item published Tex Austin’s photo of the play.

His older brother John Quinlan (Class of 1946) played on Saugus’s unbeaten 1944 football team and was inducted into the Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame in 1991. Two of Fred’s sons carried on the family’s athletic tradition at Saugus High. Fred “Freddie” Quinlan (Class of 1972) played on the football line and went on to earn All-American honors at Plymouth State. James “Jimmy” Quinlan returned to his alma mater as boys’ hockey head coach and led the Sachems to back-to-back Massachusetts Division 2 state championships in 2002–03 and 2003–04. At Bishop Fenwick, Jimmy later coached the Crusaders to their first state tournament win and a share of their first Division 1 conference title with Austin Prep.

Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1995. Fred’s grandsons made their own marks in both sports. Pat Quinlan (Class of 2002) captained the football teams at Saugus High and Plymouth State. Eric Quinlan (Class of 2004) helped lead the Sachems’ defense on both of Jimmy’s state championship teams. Eric earned a spot on the 2004 Massachusetts Public/Catholic All-Star roster and was inducted into the Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame in 2018. Jimmy and Eric are both individual Hall of Fame inductees and were also honored with the 2002–03 and 2003–04 state championship hockey teams. Together, Fred, Jimmy and Eric became the first three-generation family inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame.

alumni.name: Pat Sullivan
alumni.bio: Sullivan helped anchor the right side of the offensive line alongside Doug Mackie on Mike Ginolfi’s 1975 Sachems. The Lynn Item highlighted his blocking at guard and his play at linebacker. Sullivan was already a starting guard in 1974. Mike Ginolfi counted him among the team’s top defensive tacklers when an injury kept him out of the Thanksgiving game. Saugus went 9–1, posted six shutouts and shared the Northeastern Conference title with Salem. Sullivan was named a Lynn Item All-Star and earned NEC offensive All-Star honors on the interior line as a junior. He returned the next fall and captained the 1976 Sachems alongside Mark Calhoun. Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 2003.

alumni.name: Tom Heaney
alumni.bio: Heaney contributed to Saugus’s 6–4 team in 1974, catching a touchdown pass from Mike Burt in a 26–14 win at Danvers. A year later, he co-captained the 9–1 Northeastern Conference co-champions with Doug Mackie, John Nicolo and Steve Gannon. The 1975 game summaries document six rushing touchdowns for Heaney. He ran for two scores in the 42–16 win over Lynn English and scored Saugus’s lone touchdown on a 30-yard run against Swampscott. He also caught a two-point pass from Jay LeBranti in the 15–14 comeback at Salem. Saugus High inducted Heaney into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1993.

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Salerno
alumni.bio:
Richie Salerno played three seasons of football at Saugus High and was a senior on John Janusas’s 1953 North Shore League championship team. The yearbook noted his strong start that fall and his return from an injury suffered against Chelsea. He was back in the lineup for the 33–6 Thanksgiving win over Peabody that clinched the title and capped a 6–1–1 season.

After his playing days, Salerno returned to Sachem football as a coach. By 1971 he was teaching and coaching at Saugus High, working with students in the classroom and on the football field. He became a well-known and respected educator in Saugus and remained a familiar figure to people around the football program. Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 2004.

alumni.name: Mark Strangie
alumni.bio: A three-year starter on both sides of the line, Strangie co-captained the 1982 Sachems with Anthony Guthro and helped them rebound to 5–4–1. Picked to finish last in the Northeastern Conference after a 1–9 season, Saugus won five straight conference games and finished third. Strangie earned NEC and Lynn Item All-Star honors, and a Division 2 selection sheet also named him to its offensive line. The North roster for the 1983 Shriners Football Classic lists him as No. 70 under the spelling “Mark Strange.”
alumni.source: Saugus High yearbook and 1982 newspaper All-Star selections.

alumni.name: Joe Barressi
alumni.bio:
Barressi accounted for 103 points for the 7–3 Sachems in 1987. The senior co-captain caught nine touchdown passes, ran for two scores and returned two punts for touchdowns. He also kicked 19 extra points and two field goals. His three extra points helped decide the 21–20 Thanksgiving win over Peabody. The NEC selected him as an offensive back, and the Lynn Item named him an All-Star at defensive back. In the 1988 Agganis Classic he shared East team MVP honors. Barressi went on to Plymouth State, where he was on the football roster from 1988 through 1991, first at running back and later at wide receiver.

Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1998.

alumni.name: Larry Furey
alumni.bio:
Furey earned Northeastern Conference All-Star honors on both sides of the line in successive seasons. The conference selected him on the defensive line as a junior in 1986 and at guard as a senior in 1987. A co-captain of the 7–3 team, he recorded nine tackles and a sack against Gloucester and earned Lynn Item All-Star honors on the offensive line. The following summer he represented Saugus on the North roster for the 1988 Shriners football game, wearing No. 72.

Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2008.

alumni.name: Rob Gannon
alumni.bio:
Rob Gannon started at wide receiver and defensive back as a sophomore in 2002. He could make plays out of the backfield, too, breaking a 79-yard touchdown run against Lynn English. The 2002 Thanksgiving feature profiled him alongside his older brother John, a senior two-way starter, and their father Steve, the team’s defensive coordinator. He moved to quarterback as a junior while continuing to start on defense. In 2003, he threw two touchdown passes in a 26–13 win over Marblehead. In a 29–14 comeback win at Beverly, he threw for one two-point conversion and ran in another.

Gannon bruised his wrist against Lynn Classical late in his junior season, leaving his availability at quarterback uncertain heading into the 2003 Thanksgiving game.

Gannon shared the 2004 captaincy with Mike Nicolo and Brian Bianchi. Against Beverly that fall, he threw a 35-yard touchdown pass to Kevin Davis and scored on a one-yard run. He added a 54-yard touchdown run against Swampscott. After his senior season, he was selected for the 2005 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic.

Gannon was also a three-time Northeastern Conference All-Star in hockey and helped Saugus win back-to-back state titles in 2003 and 2004. He ran outdoor track and went on to play football and hockey at Hamilton College, where he played safety for the Continentals. Hamilton’s No. 25 recorded three solo tackles against Wesleyan and two against Bates in 2008. A 2009 NESCAC report credits him with an interception returned 11 yards through the first two games of his senior football season. Saugus High School inducted Rob into its Athletic Hall of Fame as part of the Class of 2024, following his father Steve, who was inducted in 1988.

As a sophomore in 2002, Gannon scored on a one-yard run against Winthrop and a 79-yard run against Lynn English. He intercepted a pass against Salem, recovered a fumble against Lynn Classical and came on at quarterback after halftime against Beverly.

alumni.name: Don “Donnie” Trainor
alumni.bio:
Donnie Trainor started at middle linebacker for Mike Ginolfi’s 1977 Northeastern Conference champions. He was one of four returning starters the following fall and shared the captaincy with Paul Nigro and Mike Allan. As a senior, Trainor earned Northeastern Conference All-Star honors. The Boston Globe listed him at tackle and credited him with eight unassisted tackles in a 12–7 win over Beverly. Saugus finished 6–3–1 and closed the season with a 30–14 Thanksgiving win at Peabody.

Trainor returned to coach at Saugus and worked with his younger brother Tom in the early 1980s. In the mid-1990s, he and John Nicolo helped rebuild the Saugus youth football program. At Saugus High, Trainor served as an assistant coach under head coaches John Nicolo and Mike Broderick. He coached his son Tyler and his nephews Tommy and Jack. Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1997.

alumni.name: Mark Spadafora
alumni.bio:
Mark Spadafora co-captained the 2003 Sachems and played on both lines. At right guard, he made the calls for the entire offensive line, adjusting blocking assignments when defenses shifted. His blocking helped pave the way for Mike Nicolo’s 306-yard rushing game against Salem. Spadafora earned Northeastern Conference football All-Star honors and was selected to play on both lines in the 2004 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic. He also received an Agganis Foundation scholarship.

Spadafora graduated as Saugus High’s valedictorian. The National Football Foundation and Hall of Fame selected him for its scholar-athlete award, recognizing his football and academic achievements. He was one of 22 Eastern Massachusetts football players chosen for recognition. He played basketball and earned second-team All-NEC and Academic All-American honors as a lacrosse defenseman. At MIT, he played four seasons on the offensive line and captained the football team as a senior in 2007. He was also a four-year lacrosse starter and two-time captain. After graduating from MIT with a degree in mechanical engineering, he went on to coach the Engineers’ men’s lacrosse defense.

alumni.bio:
Brian Bianchi was a three-year varsity starter who played linebacker and offensive line for the Sachems. As a junior, he helped anchor the 2003 defensive front. He shared the 2004 captaincy with Mike Nicolo and Rob Gannon and finished his senior season with 108 tackles, including eight for loss, four forced fumbles and three recoveries.

Bianchi earned 2004 Northeastern Conference and Lynn Item football All-Star honors at linebacker. After graduating in 2005, he was selected for the Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic.

alumni.name: Fred “Freddie” Quinlan
alumni.bio:
Fred “Freddie” Quinlan played on the line for Saugus High. The 1970 Tontoquonian names him in the team photo for Paul Maguire’s 1969 Sachems, who finished 7–2. His senior profile in the 1972 yearbook singled him out as one of the school’s outstanding football players.

Quinlan went on to play offensive guard at Plymouth State. The school’s football media guide credits him with NAIA All-American honors in 1974 and 1975. He also earned Associated Press Little All-America honorable mention in 1975.

His father, Fred Quinlan (Saugus High Class of 1950), was a standout running back and catcher who helped the Sachems win the 1949 Exchange Bowl. His son, Pat Quinlan (Saugus High Class of 2002), was a four-year starter on defense and a senior football captain at Saugus before becoming a defensive lineman and captain at Plymouth State.

alumni.name: Frank Serino
alumni.bio:
Frank Serino played split end and started at outside linebacker on Mike Ginolfi’s 1977 Sachems, who went 9–1 and won the Northeastern Conference title outright. He earned Lynn Item All-Star honors and a spot on the Northeastern Conference offensive All-Star team and led Eastern Massachusetts Division 2 with nine touchdown receptions. He also caught five two-point conversions and finished with 64 points.

Serino caught five passes for 58 yards and three touchdowns in a 25–7 win over Swampscott, earning Boston Globe Division 2 weekly offensive honorable mention. He caught two touchdown passes in a 28–14 win over Beverly and caught a touchdown pass from George Nicolo in the 12–0 upset of defending Division 3 Super Bowl champion Lynn Classical. On Thanksgiving, he caught six passes for 116 yards against Peabody, including George Nicolo’s go-ahead touchdown pass in the final five minutes of a 12–10 win. The Globe measured the play at 28 yards and the Item at 27. Serino then tackled Keith Wooley short of the marker on a fourth-down catch to give Saugus the ball back.

Serino also excelled at baseball at Saugus High. Years later, he coached Babe Ruth and American Legion baseball and served as an assistant baseball coach at Saugus High.

Serino was the brother of Christie “Chris” Serino, a Saugus quarterback and fellow Athletic Hall of Famer. Frank entered the Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame in 2002.

alumni.name: Paul Serino
alumni.bio:
Paul Serino played defensive back and kicked extra points for Mike Ginolfi’s 1977 Sachems. Saugus went 9–1 and won the Northeastern Conference title outright. The Boston Globe named Serino to its 1977 All-Scholastic first team at defensive back, and he also earned a spot on the NEC defensive All-Star team. The season’s scoring summaries document extra points against Gloucester, Lynn English, Danvers and Swampscott. Tom Dalton’s Thanksgiving game report also identifies Serino as a split end and records a catch from George Nicolo against Peabody.

His cousin Frank Serino earned NEC All-Star honors on offense for the same championship team. Paul graduated in 1978 and was inducted into the Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame in 2009.

alumni.name: John Coffey
alumni.bio:
John Coffey made plays on offense, defense and special teams for the 9–1 NEC champions in 1977. The Lynn Item credited him with 20 catches for 363 yards and eight interceptions. His six touchdown receptions ranked third in Eastern Massachusetts Division 2. He caught all three Saugus touchdowns in an 18–12 win at Marblehead and returned a punt 51 yards for a score in a 27–6 win at Gloucester. He also threw touchdown passes against Danvers and Salem.

Coffey made the NEC offensive All-Star team and was a Lynn Item All-Star at defensive back. He was selected for the 1978 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic.

alumni.name: Tim Fawcett
alumni.bio:
Tim Fawcett helped lead the defense for Saugus’s 1977 NEC championship team. The Lynn Item credited him with 55 tackles, 12 sacks, six fumble recoveries and a blocked punt. The Saugus coaching staff voted him player of the week three times that season. He also caught an 18-yard touchdown pass from John Coffey in the 41–6 win over Danvers.

Fawcett earned NEC All-Star honors on defense and Lynn Item All-Star honors at utility. Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1997.

alumni.name: Frank Doyle

Frank Doyle shared the 1977 captaincy with Dan Hashem and played on both lines for Mike Ginolfi’s Sachems. He started three seasons at offensive guard and two at nose guard, according to his Item All-Star profile. Saugus went 9–1, won the Northeastern Conference outright and held opponents to 88 points in ten games. The Lynn Item credited Doyle with 48 tackles, nine sacks and two fumble recoveries.

Doyle earned Lynn Item All-Star honors on the offensive line and a spot on the NEC offensive All-Star team. Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1999.

alumni.name: Joseph Bucchiere
alumni.bio:
Bucchiere kicked the decisive field goal with John Harrington holding in the 3–0 win over Class A Salem at Stackpole Field. He added two extra points in the 38–6 Thanksgiving win over Danvers. Buzz Harvey’s team finished 9–1–1 and won North Shore honors. The archive records a Boston Globe postseason selection for Bucchiere.

He converted all three extra-point attempts in the 21–0 victory over Amesbury. The decisive kick was the only field goal of his high school career, according to the 1940 yearbook. About 10,000 watched the late-scheduled Bowl Game on the Saturday before Thanksgiving.

alumni.bio:
Collette caught John “Iron Mike” Harrington’s touchdown pass for the only score in a 6–0 win over Marblehead. He earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention at end on Henry Toczylowski’s unbeaten Class C state champions.

He also delivered a 78-yard punt in the 14–7 victory over Gloucester.

alumni.name: Stanley Wladkowski
alumni.bio: Wladkowski played end on Saugus’s unbeaten 1941 Class C state championship team. The Boston Globe awarded him All-Scholastic honorable mention at end alongside teammate Claude Collette. The Sachems posted six shutouts in the ten documented games.

alumni.name: Harold “Doo” Pendlebury
alumni.bio: Pendlebury earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention at tackle on the unbeaten 1941 Class C champions. He returned as a co-captain with Lennie Flaherty in 1942 and again received Globe honorable mention as Saugus finished 7–3–1 with five shutouts. His 1943 senior yearbook identifies him as Harold “Doo” Pendlebury.

alumni.name: Lawrence “Larry” Daniels
alumni.bio: Daniels played guard on Henry Toczylowski’s unbeaten 1941 Class C state champions. Toczylowski singled out his work at guard in Robert Holbrook’s postseason interview, and the Boston Globe awarded him All-Scholastic honorable mention.

alumni.name: Leonard “Lennie” Flaherty
alumni.bio:
Flaherty earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention at guard on the 1941 Class C state champions. The following fall he co-captained the Sachems with Doo Pendlebury and earned Globe honorable mention again.

Eddie Koschei picked Flaherty at guard in Bob Walsh’s Item retrospective. The article lists 1940 next to his name, while the season archive documents his Globe honorable mention in 1941 and co-captaincy in 1942.

alumni.bio: Goss scored both Saugus touchdowns in the 12–6 Thanksgiving win over Wakefield at Stackpole Field, where about 10,000 watched the teams play to a scoreless first half. He scored from one yard in the third quarter and three yards in the fourth to help the unbeaten Class C champions close their season. The Boston Globe gave him All-Scholastic honorable mention at back.

alumni.name: Richard “Dick” Allen

He earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention, received Class B and Suburban recognition in the season records, and was selected for the North Shore All-Star game.

alumni.name: Donald “Don” Reiniger
alumni.bio: Reiniger played for the 1944 Class B state champions, who allowed just 19 regular-season points. He earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention at center and was selected at linebacker for the North Shore All-Star game. The 1945 yearbook highlighted his linebacker play throughout the championship season.

alumni.name: John Quinlan
alumni.bio:
Quinlan’s senior yearbook records four years of Saugus football. He helped the 1944 Sachems complete a 10–0 regular season and win the Class B title, and the postseason yearbook account lists him among the North Shore All-Star game selections. The 1945 yearbook singled out his tackling throughout the championship season.

His younger brother Fred Quinlan (Class of 1950) also played football for Saugus and earned induction into the school’s Athletic Hall of Fame.

The 1945 yearbook’s postseason account lists him among the Sachems chosen from a team that went 10–0 in the regular season. The 1943 yearbook praised his line play and punting against Beverly and Swampscott; the 1944 review singled out his punting throughout the championship season.

alumni.name: Bruce Waybright
alumni.bio:
Waybright played for Saugus during its 1944 Class B championship season and the yearbook lists him among the North Shore All-Star game selections. Dave Lucey’s team posted eight shutouts and capped its 10–0 regular season with a 26–0 Thanksgiving win over Wakefield, where Waybright closed the scoring with a one-yard touchdown plunge. The 1945 yearbook singled out his blocking and team spirit during the championship season.

His brother Doug Waybright (Class of 1944) co-captained the 1943 Sachems and went on to play football at Notre Dame.

alumni.name: Frank Pyszko
alumni.bio:
Pyszko was a back on Dave Lucey’s 1944 Class B state champions. He earned Boston Globe second-team All-Scholastic honors and selection to the North Shore All-Star game after Saugus went 10–0 in the regular season. The Hall of Fame roster lists his surname as Pysko, and the Globe honors record renders it Pyzsko. In 1943 he ran 65 yards for a touchdown against Woburn and threw a touchdown pass to Dan Sharp against Beverly, where he also scored on the ground. His 1944 highlights included the winning touchdown pass to Spinney at Amesbury and a 90-yard run in the separate postseason game against Peabody. In the 26–0 Thanksgiving title clincher at Wakefield, Pyszko scored on a three-yard plunge, threw a touchdown pass to Art Spinney and found him for both extra points.

alumni.name: Bob Kane
alumni.bio: Kane was a back on Saugus’s undefeated regular-season Class B champions. He received Suburban recognition and Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention. He was selected for the North Shore All-Star game, but an ankle injury kept him from playing. In 1943 he scored from three yards against Woburn and four yards against Marblehead. The 1945 yearbook singled out his running and tackling against Melrose in 1944. In the 26–0 Thanksgiving title clincher at Wakefield, Kane scored from two yards out after a Saugus interception.

alumni.name: Charles “Charlie” Woodell
alumni.bio:
Woodell played four years of Saugus football and led the 1950 Sachems with 12 touchdowns. In 1949 he caught both of Richie Nicolo’s touchdown passes in the 26–6 Thanksgiving win over Peabody. In 1950 he scored four times against Salem, twice on Thanksgiving against Peabody and caught a 38-yard touchdown from Richie Nicolo in the 30–12 Exchange Bowl win over Brockton. The Boston Globe gave him All-Scholastic honorable mention at end, and he was selected for the North Shore All-Star game.

He scored on blocked-kick returns against Chelsea and Lynn English, made five extra points against Peabody on Thanksgiving and converted after all four Saugus touchdowns in the 30–12 bowl win over Brockton. As a junior, his interception and return to the Methuen 39 set up the fourth-quarter winning drive in a 6–0 victory. He earned Northeastern Conference and Lynn Item All-Star honors and was selected for the 2001 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic.

After graduating, Gould played one season at Mount Ida College as an inside linebacker in 2001. He made 10 tackles, five solo and five assisted, against Utica on September 29.

alumni.name: Joe Attubato
alumni.bio:

At Plymouth State he played on the 1995 team that finished 10–1 and co-captained the Panthers as a senior in 1997. Plymouth State lists him as a first-team ECAC All-Star on the defensive line in 1997.

alumni.name: Eugene “Gene” Decereau

He recovered two fumbles in Saugus’s 7–0 win over Peabody, the second setting up the winning 52-yard drive. He kicked the extra point in a 7–0 win at Beverly in 1947, John Janusas’s first victory as head coach. In a 21–13 comeback against Chelsea, he recovered a fumble at the nine to set up a touchdown and kicked all three extra points. The Item selected him at left tackle on its 1947 All-Scholastic team. He also made the Boston Globe Class B team and kicked an extra point in the North Shore All-Stars’ 19–6 win over Suburban Boston at Manning Bowl. He won the Lawrence P. Daniels Memorial Trophy for the 1947 season.

alumni.name: Tom Carr
alumni.bio:
Carr earned Item and Northeastern Conference football honors for Saugus in 1961. At Bates he scored 10 touchdowns as a freshman and helped turn around the program under Bob Hatch. He earned first-team All-State honors in 1963 and 1964. From 1962 through 1965, Carr scored 30 rushing touchdowns and 213 points at Bates. The Bates record book lists 213 as the program’s career scoring record and 30 as a share of the career rushing touchdown record. Bates retired his No. 42.

The Boston Patriots selected Carr in the 13th round of the 1966 AFL draft. He played in exhibitions and spent 1966 on Boston’s taxi squad while playing for the semipro Lowell Giants. He returned to Patriots camp in 1967 and broke his jaw in an exhibition game.

Eddie Koschei singled out Carr alongside Ed Maguire among the hardest-running backs he had watched, behind Ed Shipulski. Carr’s 1961 Saugus team was led by captains Eric Wormstead and Dick Allen.

Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1993.

alumni.name: Gary Quinlan
alumni.bio:
A 1979 co-captain, Quinlan caught 26 passes for 455 yards and five touchdowns, ran 21 times for 215 yards and added 305 yards on punt and kickoff returns. A two-year starter at wide receiver and defensive back, he intercepted five passes and recovered two fumbles as a senior. On Thanksgiving, he caught a 31-yard touchdown pass from Steve Peach against Peabody. He earned Item honors at utility and Northeastern Conference recognition.

At Holy Cross, Quinlan played 43 games at wide receiver from 1980 through 1983. He averaged 18.9 yards a catch, finishing with 37 receptions for 701 yards and two touchdowns. His role grew over four seasons, from two catches as a freshman to 19 for 275 yards as a senior on the 1983 team that earned the program’s first postseason berth since 1946. He also returned 16 kickoffs for 240 yards and rushed for 58 yards, giving him 999 career all-purpose yards.

Each spring, Quinlan traded his football jersey for a spot in the Holy Cross outfield. He played baseball from 1981 through 1984, stole 17 career bases and captained the team as a senior center fielder.

Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1992.

alumni.name: Thomas F. “Tommy” Sheehan
alumni.bio:
Thomas F. Sheehan played four years of football at Saugus High, including the 1944 Class B state championship season alongside Art Spinney. As a senior quarterback in 1946, he scored twice on two-yard quarterback sneaks in an 18–0 win at Chelsea. He threw the extra-point pass to Ed Ayers against Lynn Classical. Against Swampscott he faked a handoff to George Laskey and went around right end for a 40-yard touchdown. Laskey later ran in the game’s only extra point. Sheehan handled the punting against Swampscott and helped Saugus win the field-position battle in its 7–0 upset of Peabody. Sheehan, Laskey and center Andy Forti all earned places on the 1946 North Shore All-Star squad. Saugus High inducted Sheehan into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1990.

Sheehan played baseball as a junior and senior and hockey as a senior. In the spring of 1947, as John Janusas took over the football team, a newspaper account of the Lowell scrimmage named Sheehan, Forti, Mike Harrington and Alan Campbell among those helping Janusas throughout spring practice. Sheehan went on to earn a quarterback spot at Brown in 1949. He transferred to Boston College shortly before entering the Army, served in the Korean War and completed his Boston College degree in 1956.

His senior yearbook profile already mentioned his fondness for writing mysteries. Decades later, a photograph of him carrying the ball in Saugus’s 7–0 win over Peabody at Manning Bowl appeared on the cover of one of his poetry collections. Working with longtime Saugus High English teacher John Burns, he co-edited two volumes of town history, A Gathering of Memories and Of Time and the River. Saugus honored him as its Man of the Year at Founders Day in 2022.
